fix: In 'whitish mineral gray', 'mineral gray' is the colour (a lichen colour term) and 'whitish' only modifies it. In '<modifier> <colour>' the head noun is the value.
reason: The thallus is a pale (whitish) gray, not white.
Petals white, turning yellow with age: a change over time from white to yellow on the petal.

fix: In 'with <colour> hairs' the colour belongs to the hairs, not to the organ that bears them.
reason: The capsule is pilose to sericeous with yellowish hairs. The hairs are yellowish, not the capsule.
Panicles reddish: inflorescence colour, roughly red.

fix: The narrower bearer 'involucral bract' (PO_0009045) would be better for 'bractées involucrales'.
reason: 3-4 involucral bracts; bract is a correct but broader bearer.

fix: In Carex, 'utricle' means the perigynium, not the PO fruit type 'utricle capsule fruit'. Map 'utricle' to perigynium when the taxon is Carex or another Cyperaceae.
reason: The length relation (utricles equal to the glume) is right, but the bearer is the wrong class.

fix: The lexicon lists 'compressed' as a synonym of PATO_0001485 condensed (pressed tightly together). In plant descriptions 'compressed' means flattened, or 'laterally compressed' (PATO_0002054).
reason: The seed is more or less flattened, not condensed.
The outer involucral bracts are lanceolate, and the 'outer' slot is kept.
'With minute mucro' read as petal mucronate, as the rule for 'mucro' says.

target: arrangement: sori in one row (uniseriate) on each side of the pinnule midrib
fix: '<part> in N row(s)/series' gives the number of rows, not the number of parts. Read it as arrangement or row count, never as the amount of the part.
reason: The flora says one row of sori on each side, not one sorus.

target: the lateral (secondary) veins of the leaf, amount many
fix: In '<subpart> numerous' the counted part is the subpart named (here the lateral nerves), not the organ described in the sentence.
reason: It is the lateral nerves that are very numerous, not the leaves.
Leaves numerous: many leaves.

fix: Keep position words such as 'terminal', 'uppermost' or 'lateral' on the bearer when the flora describes spikes or flowers by position.
reason: Only the terminal spike is male or androgynous. Without 'terminal' the statement is false, because the other spikes are female.
Few-flowered cymes: few flowers per inflorescence.

fix: 'within/without' means inner/outer surface and must fill the place slot. 'Without' here means outside, not absence.
reason: The corolla is white inside and purplish maroon outside. Without the place, the annotation contradicts 'white within'. Mapping purplish maroon to red is acceptable.

fix: Read 'A or B to C' as A joined to the range B–C. The first alternative must not be dropped.
reason: The annotation records only the narrowly obconic to campanulate range and leaves out 'cylindric'.
18–19 phyllaries (involucral bracts).

fix: In Selaginella, dorsal and ventral leaves are described separately. Keep 'dorsal/ventral/axillary leaves' as a position slot.
reason: The shape is said only of the dorsal leaves on branches. Reading rhomboid-ovate as an in-between shape is fine.

target: pilosity: glabrous to pubescent (range), place: outside
fix: Read 'glabrous to ± pubescent' as a range or alternative that includes glabrous, not as approximately pubescent.
reason: The corolla may be glabrous outside. The annotation keeps only the pubescent end and loses 'outside'.
Leaf blade adaxially pubescent: the adaxial (upper) surface is pubescent.

fix: In Euphorbia herbs the 'rootstock' is often a woody root crown rather than a true rhizome. PO has no closer class, so this is acceptable.
reason: A lignified rootstock is woody; rootstock is a PO synonym of rhizome.

fix: When 'axis' is named under Inflorescences, the bearer is the inflorescence axis, not the whole inflorescence.
reason: The 100-300 mm length is given for the raceme axis. The numbers and the (50-) minimum are right.

target: trichome (hairs) on branch; colour grayish yellow; stage young
fix: In '<colour> pubescent/hairy/tomentose' the colour belongs to the hairs, not to the organ.
reason: The branches are pubescent with grayish yellow hairs when young; the branch surface itself is not described as grayish yellow.
The calyx segments (sepals) are 3-veined: 3 vascular bundles in each sepal.
1 or 2 flowers at each node.

fix: Ideally keep 'uppermost' as position; as an 'or' the statement still holds for all spikes.
reason: The uppermost spikes are lanceolate or cylindric, and the other spikes are cylindric, so the 'or' is not false.

target: narrowed toward the base (reduced lower pinnae), e.g. tapered PATO_0001500 — not abruptly narrowed
fix: In fern blades, 'base (slightly) contracted' means the lamina narrows toward the base because the lower pinnae are shorter. The 'contracted' synonym of FLOPO_0991316 should not fire when the degree word 'slightly' is present, because 'slightly' contradicts 'abruptly'.
reason: 'Slightly contracted' is not a sudden narrowing.

target: place: near the upper nodes (only for pubescent)
fix: In 'A or B near X', the place applies to B and must be kept in B's slot.
reason: The stem is pubescent only near the upper nodes. Saying the stem is pubescent, without the place, says too much.
6-8 stamens.

fix: The abaxial (lower) side could be added as place.
reason: The midvein is yellowish on the lower side; the colour is said only of that side.
